name: Pelvic Arteriovenous Malformation

criteria.description: Definitive visualization of abnormal arteriovenous shunting in the pelvic region by angiography or cross-sectional imaging
Presence of pelvic bruit or thrill on physical examination
Symptoms consistent with pelvic AVM such as high-output cardiac failure or localized swelling
Exclusion of other vascular malformations or tumors by imaging and clinical correlation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of imaging-confirmed abnormal arteriovenous shunting in the pelvis plus at least one major clinical criterion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging modalities such as digital subtraction angiography, CT angiography, or MRI angiography.

pathognomonic.notes: Audible or palpable turbulent blood flow over the pelvic region
searchTerms: abnormal pelvic blood vessel sound or vibration
vascular bruit or thrill in pelvis
pelvic blood flow abnormality felt or heard

pathognomonic.symptomName: High-output cardiac failure secondary to pelvic AVM
searchTerms: heart failure from high blood flow in pelvic vessels
high-output cardiac failure due to pelvic AVM
excessive cardiac workload from pelvic vascular malformation

common.symptomName: Pelvic pain localized to AVM site
common.notes: Often described as a dull, aching pain
searchTerms: pain in pelvis at vascular malformation site

common.notes: May fluctuate with position or exertion
searchTerms: visible or felt pelvic lump or swelling
pelvic mass that can be seen or touched

common.symptomName: Lower extremity edema due to venous congestion
searchTerms: leg swelling from poor venous return
lower limb edema due to vein congestion

common.notes: If AVM involves urinary tract structures

occasional.symptomName: Lower abdominal fullness or pressure sensation
searchTerms: fullness or pressure feeling in lower abdomen

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue related to chronic high-output cardiac failure
searchTerms: fatigue related to high-output cardiac failure
chronic fatigue due to heart overload

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms secondary to pelvic nerve compression
rare.notes: Including numbness or paresthesia in lower limbs
searchTerms: nerve problems due to pelvic compression

rare.symptomName: Ulceration or skin necrosis overlying AVM
rare.notes: Due to ischemia or venous hypertension
searchTerms: skin ulcers over blood vessel malformation
open sores on abnormal blood vessels

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in cases with high-output cardiac failure
imaging: Digital subtraction angiography showing early venous filling and nidus of abnormal vessels
MRI/MRA demonstrating tangled vascular structures in the pelvis
CT angiography revealing dilated feeding arteries and draining veins
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; usually sporadic
other: Physical exam findings of palpable thrill or audible bruit over pelvic region

distinguishingFeatures: Dilated pelvic veins without arteriovenous shunting
Absence of palpable thrill or bruit
Benign vascular tumor with slow flow
No direct arteriovenous communication on imaging
Solid uterine masses without vascular shunting
No bruit or thrill on examination

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe pelvic pain with signs of hemorrhagic shock
Neurological deficits in lower extremities indicating nerve compression
references: Lee BB, et al. Diagnosis and treatment of pelvic arteriovenous malformations. J Vasc Surg Venous Lymphat Disord. 2019;7(4):555-563.
